title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. Page 88 defines a 'π-fibration' (bijective) of groupoids f: C → C' for a discrete abelian group π. f is surjective on objects and on arrows. Each fibre is a connected groupoid with commutative fundamental group, identified with π. Equivalently, π maps to End(id_{C'}), each x gives an exact sequence 1 → π → Aut_C(x) → Aut_{C'}(f(x)) → 1, and π_0(f) is a bijection. A margin calls this a central extension of C' by π. Page 88 then starts an example: U a connected, locally 1-connected topological group, and P a U_T-torsor (a principal U-bundle) over a space T, with p: P → T.

This page finishes the example. Take the connected components T_i of T, put P_i = P|T_i, choose x_i in P_i with image t_i in T_i, and set π = π_1(U,1), which is abelian because U is a topological group. The homotopy sequence of the fibration gives π → π_1(P_i;x_i) → π_1(T_i;t_i) → 1; surjectivity holds because U is connected.
- If all the maps π → π_1(P_i,x_i) are injective, then Π_1(p): Π_1(P) → Π_1(T) carries a π-structure, i.e. it is a π-fibration (central extension of fundamental groupoids). Centrality holds because the image of π_1 of a connected structure group is central in π_1 of the total space.
- If these maps are not injective but their kernels N_i are independent of i, then Π_1(p) is a π'-fibration with π' = π/N_i.
- A marginal NB seems to say that connectedness of U, or the hypothesis on P, need only hold locally on T, giving a π-structure fibrewise. This is largely illegible.

Second construction (continued on p. 90), a discretisation of the base points. Take a group μ acting on a set E, a homomorphism i_μ: μ → U, and a μ-equivariant map i_E: E → P.
- Let C' be the groupoid on the object set E induced from Π_1(P), with Hom_{C'}(x,y) = Hom_{Π_1(P)}(i_E x, i_E y). By transport of structure μ acts on C'.
- Let E_0 = E/μ map to T = P/U, and let C be the groupoid on E_0 induced from Π_1(T).
- This gives a commutative square C' → Π_1(P) over C → Π_1(T). The horizontal maps are equivalences when E meets every component.
- The aim is to make f: C' → C a π-fibration (central extension) on a small, 'combinatorial' set of base points.
- A margin notes that if μ acts freely on P (i_μ injective), it acts freely on E.

The intended application in this dossier is to Teichmüller groupoids. Plausibly U = (S^1)^ν or (C*)^ν, acting on tangent directions at the marked points, and P → T is the bundle of tangential data over Teichmüller/moduli space. Then π = Z^ν (the boundary Dehn twists) gives the central extension of the Teichmüller groupoid T_{g,ν} by Z^ν. E would be a finite set of 'tangential base points' stable under a finite group μ (e.g. roots of unity μ_n ⊂ S^1). This application is not written on the page; it is inferred from the dossier title and the notation μ.
errors: The machine transcription reads 'on suppose que les hom. π → π_1(P_i;x_i) soient surjectifs'. The image and the following parenthesis ('n'est pas supposé injectif') show the hypothesis is injectivity. Surjectivity would make no sense here.
Minor gap: the exact sequence should start with π_2(T_i) → π. Grothendieck writes only the relevant part, which is harmless.

Minor gap: centrality of the image of π_1(U) in π_1(P_i) and fibrewise connectedness are used but not justified on the page. Both are standard for principal bundles with connected locally 1-connected structure group.

ideas.what: π-fibration of groupoids = central extension of a groupoid by a discrete abelian group (banded π-gerbe over a groupoid)
ideas.modern_name: central extension of groupoids / abelian band, π-gerbe
ideas.usually_credited_to: Giraud (non-abelian cohomology, 1971); Breen; R. Brown and others for groupoid extensions
ideas.where_published: related notions in SGA1/SGA4 and Giraud's thesis (supervised by Grothendieck); not this exact formulation

ideas.what: A principal U-bundle with connected U gives a central extension of fundamental groupoids Π_1(P) → Π_1(T) by π_1(U), or by a quotient π_1(U)/N
ideas.modern_name: homotopy exact sequence of a principal bundle; centrality of the image of π_1 of the structure group

ideas.what: Restricting fundamental groupoids to a small equivariant set of base points E → P with a compatible group μ → U, and passing to quotients E/μ → P/U to get a central extension on discrete base points
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid on a set of base points (Brown); equivariant tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown (fundamental groupoid on a set of base points, 1967); Deligne (tangential base points, 1989)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), on Teichmüller groupoids with base points chosen in a 'well-chosen' combinatorial way

missed.claim: The page records the setup by which Grothendieck planned to get central extensions of Teichmüller groupoids by Z^ν on a finite equivariant set of base points with a μ-action (μ presumably roots of unity). This is a discretised, equivariant version of the tangential-base-point construction later used by Moore–Seiberg, Bakalov–Kirillov, Funar–Gelca and Nakamura–Schneps. The mathematics itself is standard, and the application is only implicit here.
missed.quote: Soit, dans l'exemple précédent, E un ensemble ... μ --i_μ--> U un hom. de groupes, et E --i_E--> P une application, compatible avec les opérations de μ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's own framework for central extensions of the Teichmüller tower (the S0 T_{g,ν} objects) before the 1984 Esquisse. This is of historical interest, but not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine, correct example: principal bundles give central extensions of fundamental groupoids, followed by an equivariant restriction to discrete base points. It is historically relevant as groundwork for Teichmüller groupoids with tangential base points, but contains nothing a specialist would find unknown.
transcription_corrections: 'on suppose que les hom. π → π_1(P_i;x_i) soient surjectifs' should read 'soient injectifs'.
The first line is likely 'alors pour les comp. connexes T_i de T'. The exact sequence ends with π_1(T_i; t_i) → 1, not π_1(M̄_i; t_i').
Left margin: 'x_i ∈ P_i = P|T_i, t_i image dans T_i'. The 'U_i' in the transcription is likely 'T_i'.
'Soit, dans l'exemple précédent, E un ensemble' probably continues as '... μ un groupe qui opère sur E'.
Left margin: 'p: P → T surjection ... fibres connexes'. This is roughly as transcribed but uncertain.
